saints.name: St. Genevieve
saints.title: Virgin, Patroness of Paris
saints.shortBlurb: The consecrated virgin whose prayers and courage steadied Paris through the terror of the barbarian invasions…
biography: Born about 419 at Nanterre, a village west of Paris, Genevieve was a child when Germanus of Auxerre, passing through on his way to Britain about 429, discerned her calling; at fifteen she was consecrated to God as a virgin, and after her parents' death she made her home in Paris.

When Attila and his Huns swept into Gaul in 451 and the terrified citizens prepared to flee, Genevieve persuaded the people of Paris to remain, to fast, and to pray, and the city was spared, the invader turning aside toward Orléans. In 464, when Childeric the Frank besieged Paris, she led a convoy of boats up the Seine to fetch grain and won mercy for prisoners.

She died in great old age about 512 and was buried in the church of Saints Peter and Paul, raised by King Clovis at her urging, which became the abbey of Sainte-Geneviève. For twice standing between the city and its destroyers she is venerated as the patroness of Paris.
saints.knownFor: Encouraging Paris to trust in God during the invasions of Attila.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 3 January
